about: The Ark's behaviour checks in CI (.github/workflows/ark-behaviour-audit.yml, scripts/ark-audit-check.mts). Each limit is the merged ark-release value on 2026-11-11 (877ae2c5, the CI configuration below) with a small slack: they stop a regression, not demand the final targets (docs/ark/behaviour-audit.md). Raise them by hand as the lanes improve the numbers; a deliberate worsening changes the limit in the same PR, with why. `--write` prints today's values.

config.measured: 877ae2c5: flyers 596, circling 0.1%, turns 0.78/min, non-flocking followers 0, never move 760, graze label 28.6%, never grazed 39, amphibians crossing 435, snapped 0, heads near camera 99.8%, predators with prey within 5 m at spawn 162, prey react 97% / flee 63.5% near camera (median 0.2 s), awake all-same 14.1%, always in step 80, distinct 2.08, wrong surface 1.3%, sinking 11; encounters react 61.7%, close flee 56.7%, median 0.1 s, heads turn 81.3%

checks.why: Decision 285 (2026-11-13, MA1 follow-up): the hawkers (swallows, martins, swifts: intelligence hunt aerial_hawk) are counted apart. Hawking turns over a feeding patch by design and was all of the circling on main d8ee89f0 (2.2% of air time, the rest 0.0%); with every other flight at its true speed instead of a crawl (main's wood pigeon was aloft 41% of an hour at 0.17 m/s) the island-wide share was set by how briefly the rest were up. All flyers: main 2.2%, ark-flight-physics-2 3.0%; all but the hawkers: main 0.0%, ark-flight-physics-2 0.0%. Decision 287 (the integrator): this split replaces main's all-flyers circling limit of 2.8 (decision 285's round, 486cb701), which counted the hawkers in.

checks.why: Decision 285: as the circling, the hawkers apart. All flyers: main 0.64, ark-flight-physics-2 1.26; all but the hawkers: main 0.24, ark-flight-physics-2 0.67 (a range-boxed bird's own flight is now a round out and back, half a turn in about 40 s, where it was a crawl about its spot).

checks.id: hawkers: air time circling (%)
checks.why: Decision 285: the hawkers guarded on their own at today's value. Main d8ee89f0 26.0% of 28,081 s aloft, ark-flight-physics-2 36% of 18,739 s: about the same circling (7,292 s against about 6,750 s), less time up between their hawking (their transit flights at their true speed). Lane B3 needs (the behaviours pass, 2026-11-14; main c99ff83b against ark-beh-needs, the same CI configuration): 36.0% of 18,743 s aloft -> 53.9% of 20,543 s. Deliberate: a swallow or a swift now feeds through 70% of its waking time, as the birds do, where every species fed a third of its slots; its feeding is hawking, which turns over a patch by design, so more of its air time is hawking (about 6,750 s -> 11,070 s) and less is transit.

near camera: prey that react to a hunter (%)
checks.why: The behaviours pass, lane B2 (2026-11-14, docs/ark/behaviour-pass-2026-11/prey.md): 97.5 on main c99ff83b -> 92 on ark-beh-prey a63e34e8 (219 of 238). Deliberate changes of rule: who is a threat goes by body mass as well as the food links (the audit's own table of hunters is by the food links alone), and an animal with its head down sees a predator only when it next looks up. The 19 that did not react were not broken down further.

checks.id: near camera: prey that flee a hunter (%)
checks.why: The behaviours pass, lane B2 (2026-11-14): 71.8 on main c99ff83b -> 42.9 on ark-beh-prey a63e34e8 (102 of 238). Deliberate: prey run from a predator coming, creeping or chasing, or one inside a shorter distance when it is lying up (0.6 of the flight distance) or walking by; the rest watch it, walk off, close up, stand their ground, hold still or pull in, and then tolerate it. Near the camera the time spent in 'flee' went from 33.2% to 4% (a flight is a dash, then a stop), 'alert' from 46.4% to 57.4% (the audit's stops are 35 s from a fresh layer beside a hunter: most of each is the first watch), looking round from 9.4% to 22.8%, feeding from 5.5% to 7.2%.

encounters: prey that react (%)
encounters: close prey that flee (%)
checks.why: The behaviours pass, lane B2 (2026-11-14, docs/ark/behaviour-pass-2026-11/prey.md): 58.9 on main c99ff83b -> 38.9. Deliberate: the response now fits what the predator is doing. A predator standing still 4 m off is run from by 17.3% of prey (50.7% before: its flight distance is 0.6 of the rule's, the rest walk off or keep where they are and tolerate it); one walking past at 2 to 4 m by 49.7% (63%: the sighting itself no longer counts as a predator remembered, which had made every flight distance 1.25 times its rule); armed and dominant animals stand their ground, cryptic ones hold still, armoured ones pull in (any defence of its own: 62.9% -> 56.9%). The pairs are now the layer's own (food links and body mass).

checks.id: encounters: median seconds to react
checks.why: The behaviours pass, lane B2 (2026-11-14): 0.1 on main c99ff83b -> 0.67. The clock starts when the predator comes within 25 m. Before, a prey animal that had seen it further off was still staring at it then (0 s); now it has watched it, settled and gone back to feeding, and its next look at the predator is what is timed (walking past: 0 -> 1.57 s; standing still: 0.23 -> 0.47 s).

checks.id: awake moments a whole group does the same (%)
checks.why: Lane B3 needs (the behaviours pass, 2026-11-14; main c99ff83b against ark-beh-needs, the same CI configuration): 14.0% -> 16.9%. Deliberate: each kind has its own day in bouts, so a kind that feeds 60 to 80% of its waking time (a zebra, an elephant, a tit) is all feeding at once more often than when every species fed a third of its slots drawn one by one. Members keep up to three tenths of a feeding cycle off their leader and one of a group is on watch; mean distinct states in a group of 4 is 2.10 (2.16), species always in step 82 (82).
